correctness.rationale: An exhibited prime in each of twelve classes bounds its least possible prime by \(6165527\). The Eratosthenes scan enumerates every smaller candidate, including all primes and offsets; prime-square marking is equivalent to nonsquarefreeness because a repeated prime has square <= n. A second integer-trial square-factor predicate produces identical minima; displayed primes and each four-square divisor are trial-division checked. Small excluded primes 5 and 7 have an initial squarefree remainder. Deterministic Python 3 certificate replayed successfully with VERIFY_OK. The exact scope is first failures for \(a=0\),1,2,3, not an infinite assertion.

originality.rationale: The twelve-class sharp first-prime table for four power-of-two shifts is not mathematically implied by the inspected published results: the source arXiv paper restricts its theorem to one class and density, Hercher treats odd integers and \(a\ge1\) with different record tables, and checked OEIS tables use different domains/shifts. Ten focused published-results index searches returned no matching or stronger result, and accessible past mathematical claims were checked for overlap. Database nonappearance is not a novelty proof: the arXiv full text could not be read, and unindexed numerical work is a residual risk.
residual_risks: Harman–Paquin preprint complete PDF/appendix was inaccessible despite arXiv/HTML and mirror attempts. Its class-7 numerical dataset might cover that row, although its available theorem is restricted to one class.
An unpublished, unindexed, or obscure table of all twelve minima may exist; semantic search is not mathematical proof of originality.
The finding deliberately asserts no novelty for the already known density or existence results and no standalone novelty for any previously tabulated individual numeral.

value.rationale: The first four powers in the Erdős squarefree decomposition problem produce natural local strata modulo \(\operatorname{lcm}(4,9)=36\); the current motivating paper explicitly studies one of those 12 classes. The complete sharp first-prime table, with a 1200-fold spread, is a natural finite invariant and a quantitative benchmark for each stratum, rather than an arbitrary sampled interval, an unmotivated slice, or a restatement of a density theorem. A general downstream theorem is not asserted or needed.
